newsitem.title: USA: US Democrats ask Clinton to hold line on tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: US Democrats ask Clinton to hold line on tax cuts.

text.p: A group of Democrat senators have sent President Clinton a letter asking him to hold the line on tax cuts in budget talks with congressional Republicans, one of the senators said Thursday.

"It is quite possible that if we forego tax cuts altogether, or even if we enact very limited and targeted tax relief, we could balance the budget by 2001," the letter said, according to a statement from Dale Bumpers, an Arkansas Democrat.

A total of 15 senators co-signed the letter, including Senate Democrat Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota and Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan of New York who is the ranking Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, Bumpers said.

"The time to balance the budget, Mr. President, is now, while the economy is strong. We should not let tax cuts force us to wait and risk an economic downturn which makes deficit reduction impossible," the letter said.
